tools.description: Get top API keys ranked by a metric. Each result: organization_key_id, organization_key_name, number_of_requests, total_cost (USD), total_tokens, avg_latency (seconds), error_count. Only keys that appear in logs for the time range. filters.description: Filter the input population BEFORE ranking/summarizing. Shape: {"<field>": {"operator": "<op>", "value": "<val>"}}. CRITICAL: operator "" (empty string) means EXACT EQUALITY — pass it as a literal empty string, NOT a placeholder. Filterable fields and their semantics: "provider_id" — provider slug for provider-scoped questions. Canonical slugs: "anthropic", "openai", "azure_openai", "bedrock", "google_gemini_ai", "google_vertex_ai", "cohere", "deepseek", "fireworks", "groq", "mistral", "moonshot", "openrouter", "perplexity", "together_ai", "xai", "cerebras". NOTE the underscored compound forms — "google" is NOT a slug (use "google_gemini_ai" or "google_vertex_ai"); "vertex" is NOT a slug (use "google_vertex_ai"); "azure" is NOT a slug (use "azure_openai"). REQUIRED when the user names a specific provider; without it the tool returns a global ranking/summary across ALL providers, which is the wrong answer for provider-scoped questions. If the user says "Google" without specifying Gemini vs Vertex, ask which one or call separately for both and combine. Example: {"provider_id": {"operator": "", "value": "anthropic"}}. "model" — specific model string; used for model-name filtering, NOT provider filtering. Use operator "icontains" for model — stored names carry version/date suffixes ("gpt-5.1-2025-11-13"), so an exact match on "gpt-5.1" misses most logs. "organization_key_id" — UUID of an API key (resolve a user-given key name via api_key_list first; this field never accepts names). "customer_identifier" — end-user/customer tag string. "deployment_name" — deployment slug string. This filter IS supported on every dashboard tool whose schema exposes a `filters` parameter (the dashboard_top_* family, dashboard_llm_metrics_over_time, dashboard_llm_metrics_summary, dashboard_metric_chart, dashboard_active_users, dashboard_quantiles_over_time, dashboard_quantiles_summary); never tell the user a tool that has this parameter cannot filter by these fields.

tools.name: automation_create
tools.description: An automation runs a task sequence against incoming telemetry — this is the online-eval surface. This is the data on the Automations page. RETURNS: id (version PK), workflow_id (family ID — pass it as automation_id to automation_get / automation_update), version, name, tasks. Task types: condition (filter/gate), sampling (random %), eval (run a grader), ingest (save to dataset), webhook (HTTP callback), notification (email/Slack/PagerDuty), aggregation (time-window metrics), switch (multi-branch routing), compute (arithmetic on upstream outputs). Task ordering: gates first (condition, sampling) then aggregation then actions (notification, webhook, eval, ingest). TRIGGER MAPPING: 'spans'/'logs'/'requests' to request_log; 'completed traces'/'traces' to trace_completed. UI CONVENTION: tasks MUST start with a sampling task whose id is LITERALLY 'auto-sampling' (type='sampling', config.rate 0.0-1.0, default 1). The top-level 'Run workflow on X% of incoming' control is backed by that exact task id. '+ Add task' palette (what the user sees): condition (Filtering), aggregation, compute (Computation), switch, webhook, ingest (Dataset), eval (Evaluator). HIDDEN from that menu but still valid and executable: notification, prompt, completion, throttle. If you include a hidden-type task, your final message MUST state which inlined tasks are not in the '+ Add task' menu.

name.description: Workflow name — a clean descriptive title (e.g., 'Error Spike Alert'), never the user's raw request sentence.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this automation does

is_enabled.description: IGNORED by the server (read-only field) — automations are always created disabled. Make one live with automation_commit + automation_deploy.

trigger_event_type.description: Event type this automation is designed to handle. UI wording → enum: 'spans'/'logs'/'requests' → request_log; 'completed traces'/'traces' → trace_completed; 'eval result' → on_eval_result_ingested. 'scheduled' (the reports trigger) fires on schedule_cron instead of an event and REQUIRES schedule_cron.

schedule_cron.description: UTC cron schedule, standard 5-field syntax (e.g. '0 9 * * 1' = Mondays 09:00 UTC). REQUIRED when trigger_event_type='scheduled', rejected otherwise. No seconds field, no TZ=/CRON_TZ= prefix, minimum 5 minutes between fires. A scheduled automation only fires once a committed version is enabled.

tasks.description: Ordered list of automation tasks. Chain via `next`. If type='automations', FIRST task MUST be {id:'auto-sampling', type:'sampling', label:'<pct>% sampling', config:{rate:<0-1>}, next:'<first-user-task-id>'}. Then: gates (condition, switch) → aggregation/compute → actions (webhook, ingest, eval).

id.description: Unique task id — a short slug like 'agg', 'filter_failed', 'notify', NOT a UUID. It surfaces in 'next' pointers, switch targets, state.<task_id>.* dotpaths, and notification templates.

type.description: Task type. get_logs/get_traces/limit_breaches/get_pulse/pulse_summarize are REPORT building blocks — use them in type='reports' automations with trigger_event_type='scheduled'.

label.description: Optional human-readable label for the task (e.g., 'Cost aggregation (5m)').

next.description: REQUIRED for task chaining. ID of the next task to execute after this one succeeds. Without 'next', the automation STOPS after this task (no sequential fallback). Example: if task A should flow to task B, set A's next to B's id.

config.description:
Task-specific configuration. Required fields per type:

NAMESPACE: Every task evaluates against a namespace with 4 keys: event (original log, flattened), input (previous task output), state (all upstream results keyed by task id/label), context (org/automation metadata). Condition/switch field names are dotpaths: 'event.status', 'state.<task_id>.cost_sum'. Simple field names do NOT work — always prefix with event./state.

CONDITION → condition_policy: {dotpath_field: {operator, value}} for inline rules. FIELD NAMES MUST use namespace dotpath prefix:
• Event fields: 'event.status', 'event.cost', 'event.model', 'event.latency', etc.
• Upstream task output: 'state.<task_id>.cost_sum', 'state.<task_id>.score', etc.
NEVER use 'input.<field>' in condition_policy — the frontend cannot render it. Always use 'state.<task_id>.<field>' to reference upstream task output. Policy keys ARE the dotpath field names — a binary-expression object ({'left': <field>, 'right': <value>, 'operator': <op>}) is rejected at save time.
OPERATOR RULES BY FIELD TYPE:
• Categorical (status, status_code, model, provider_id, log_type, deployment_name): ALWAYS 'in' with array: {"event.model": {"operator": "in", "value": ["gpt-4o"]}}. Exclude with 'not': {"event.status": {"operator": "not", "value": ["failed"]}}.
• Numeric (cost, latency, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_request_tokens): 'lte'/'gte'/'gt'/'lt' for ranges: {"event.cost": {"operator": "gte", "value": 0.01}}.
• Boolean (stream, cache_bit, has_tool_calls, is_root_span, positive_feedback): 'in' with array: {"event.stream": {"operator": "in", "value": [true]}}.
• Text (customer_identifier, thread_identifier, custom_identifier, group_identifier, prompt_id, prompt_name, span_name, span_workflow_name): 'icontains', 'startswith', 'in', 'not', 'empty', 'not_empty'.
NEVER use '' (empty string) or '=' as operator. Status values: 'failed' (errors), 'success', 'warning'. OR condition_id (str) for saved conditions. Also: on_true (default 'continue'), on_false (default 'stop').
Output: {triggered: bool, triggered_metrics: [...]}.

SAMPLING → rate: float 0.0-1.0 (e.g., 0.1 = 10% of events). Output: passthrough (input forwarded to next task).

EVAL → evaluator_id: str (UUID from evaluator_list). Output: {score, evaluator_name, ...} (evaluation results).

INGEST → target_type: 'dataset'|'log'|'experiment', target: {dataset_id: '<uuid>'} or {experiment_id: '<uuid>'} or {} (for log), source: 'event' (default) | 'input' | 'state.<task_id>'. Output: confirmation with ingested ID.

NOTIFICATION → notification_method_id: str (UUID from notification_method_list), severity: 'low'|'medium'|'high'|'urgent', message_template: str with LITERAL double-brace Jinja2 placeholders (you MUST wrap each variable name in double curly braces — e.g. '{{automation_name}} alert: cost is ${{cost}}'). Available variables: automation_name, model, status, error_message, status_code, cost, latency, customer_identifier, prompt_name, severity. For aggregation output: <output_field_name> (e.g. cost_sum, error_count). Notification flattens the full namespace as template variables automatically.
Output: {dispatch_results, notifications_sent}.

WEBHOOK → webhook_url: str (required), webhook_secret: str (optional), is_including_scores: bool (optional), source: 'event' (default) | 'input' | 'state.<task_id>' (optional). Output: {webhook_url, dispatched: bool}.

AGGREGATION → time_step_minutes: int 1-10080 (default 5), metrics: [{field_name, aggregation_function: sum|avg|count|max|min, output_field_name (ALWAYS include — use field_function format, e.g. cost_sum, latency_avg; when omitted the output key auto-names <field_name>_<aggregation_function> — cost/avg → cost_avg, NEVER avg_cost), filters (optional per-metric pre-filter, applied per event before the metric increments)}].
AGGREGATION metric filters use the SAME shape as condition_policy above — {dotpath_field: {operator, value}}, e.g. {"event.status": {"operator": "in", "value": ["failed"]}} — and the SAME operator rules by field type: categorical and boolean take 'in'/'not' with an ARRAY value, numeric take 'gte'/'lte'/'gt'/'lt', text takes 'icontains'/'startswith'/'in'/'not'/'empty'/'not_empty'. Field names need the namespace dotpath prefix (event.*). WARNING: unlike condition and switch policies, metric filters are NOT validated at save time. A binary-expression object ({'left': ..., 'right': ..., 'operator': ...}) or any other wrong shape saves cleanly and then silently matches NOTHING at runtime, so the metric aggregates zero events and the downstream threshold never fires. Get the shape right on the first write.
For broad event filtering, use a condition task BEFORE aggregation. In type='monitors' automations, aggregation defaults is_comparing_to_previous=true (output includes % change vs the previous window; explicit false opts out; not defaulted when a metric uses max/min). Output: {aggregated_values: {<output_field_name>: value}, is_finished: {<field>: bool}}.

SWITCH → cases: array of case objects, each with EITHER {condition_id: '<uuid>', target: '<task_id>'} (saved condition) OR {condition_policy: {dotpath_field: {operator, value}}, target: '<task_id>'} (inline condition). First matching case wins. default: fallback target task id (optional). Switch evaluates against namespace (same dotpath rules as condition). Switch routes via case targets — does NOT need 'next' field.

COMPUTE → function: 'ratio'|'percentage'|'difference'|'weighted_average' (required), inputs: [{source: 'state.<task_id>', field: '<field_name>', weight: <float>}] (required). Binary functions (ratio, percentage, difference) take exactly 2 operands. weighted_average takes 2+ operands with weight field. label: optional human-readable name. Output: {result: <number>}.

PROMPT → prompt_id: str (UUID from prompt_list — NEVER pass a prompt name like 'Math Tutor' as prompt_id; call prompt_list first and use the returned id field), version: int (optional), override_params: object (optional model/temperature/max_tokens overrides). Loads the prompt template, renders variables from the input namespace, and runs an LLM completion. Output: {input, output, metrics: {cost, latency, tokens}}.

COMPLETION → model: str (LLM name, required, e.g. 'gpt-4o-mini'), temperature/max_tokens/top_p (optional). Sends input messages directly to the LLM without a template. Output: {input, output, metrics: {cost, latency, tokens}}.

THROTTLE → cooldown_seconds: int 1-86400 (required). Fires once per cooldown window and suppresses subsequent firings until the window elapses. Typical placement: after a threshold condition, before a notification/webhook, to prevent alert spam.

REPORT TASKS (type='reports' + trigger_event_type='scheduled' only; the digest window is anchored to the span since the previous scheduled fire):

GET_LOGS → window_seconds: int (required, ≤ 604800 = 7 days; fallback when no previous-fire anchor exists), metrics: array of DASHBOARD_METRICS names (required, e.g. number_of_requests, total_cost, total_tokens, error_count, error_percentage, average_cost, average_latency, average_ttft, unique_customers; max_tpm is rejected), group_by: array of bare CHLogV3 columns (organization_key_id, model, provider_id, environment, customer_identifier, prompt_id, status_code; empty = one summary row; a multi-element list is ONE composite grouping), breakdowns: array of column lists — independent per-dimension rollups, mutually exclusive with group_by (max 10), order_by: {field, direction} (optional, defaults first-metric desc), max_groups: int (default 100), include_prior_period: bool (adds prior-window totals for delta rendering). No custom metadata.X paths and no filtering — the slice is org + window.

GET_TRACES → trace-level sibling of get_logs over the trace agg table. window_seconds + metrics required; metrics from TRACE_METRICS (trace_count, total_cost, average_cost_per_trace, total_tokens, average_tokens_per_trace, error_count, average_duration, max_duration, average_spans_per_trace); group_by limited to organization_key_id, environment, customer_identifier (no model — a trace spans multiple models). No breakdowns / include_prior_period.

LIMIT_BREACHES → reports live limit-policy breaches at fire time (no window). scope: 'api_key' (only supported value, default), max_rows: int (default 50). Config may be empty {}.

GET_PULSE → pulls the report window's error-issue pulse facts for downstream summarization. max_issues: int (default 10), window_seconds: int (optional fallback when no previous-fire anchor — set to the same value as the report's get_logs tasks). Config may be empty {}.

PULSE_SUMMARIZE → LLM summary of upstream get_pulse facts. No config knobs — pass config {} and chain it directly after a get_pulse task.

NAMESPACE: Every task evaluates against a namespace with 4 keys: event (original log, flattened), input (previous task output), state (all upstream results keyed by task id/label), context (org/automation metadata). • Upstream task output: 'state.<task_id>.cost_sum', 'state.<task_id>.score', etc.

Policy keys ARE the dotpath field names — a binary-expression object ({'left': <field>, 'right': <value>, 'operator': <op>}) is rejected at save time.

• Categorical (status, status_code, model, provider_id, log_type, deployment_name): ALWAYS 'in' with array: {"event.model": {"operator": "in", "value": ["gpt-4o"]}}. Exclude with 'not': {"event.status": {"operator": "not", "value": ["failed"]}}.
• Numeric (cost, latency, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_request_tokens): 'lte'/'gte'/'gt'/'lt' for ranges: {"event.cost": {"operator": "gte", "value": 0.01}}.
• Boolean (stream, cache_bit, has_tool_calls, is_root_span, positive_feedback): 'in' with array: {"event.stream": {"operator": "in", "value": [true]}}.
• Text (customer_identifier, thread_identifier, custom_identifier, group_identifier, prompt_id, prompt_name, span_name, span_workflow_name): 'icontains', 'startswith', 'in', 'not', 'empty', 'not_empty'.
NEVER use '' (empty string) or '=' as operator. Status values: 'failed' (errors), 'success', 'warning'. OR condition_id (str) for saved conditions. Also: on_true (default 'continue'), on_false (default 'stop').
Output: {triggered: bool, triggered_metrics: [...]}.

SAMPLING → rate: float 0.0-1.0 (e.g., 0.1 = 10% of events). Output: passthrough (input forwarded to next task).

EVAL → evaluator_id: str (UUID from evaluator_list). Output: {score, evaluator_name, ...} (evaluation results).

INGEST → target_type: 'dataset'|'log'|'experiment', target: {dataset_id: '<uuid>'} or {experiment_id: '<uuid>'} or {} (for log), source: 'event' (default) | 'input' | 'state.<task_id>'. Output: confirmation with ingested ID.

NOTIFICATION → notification_method_id: str (UUID from notification_method_list), severity: 'low'|'medium'|'high'|'urgent', message_template: str with LITERAL double-brace Jinja2 placeholders (you MUST wrap each variable name in double curly braces — e.g. '{{automation_name}} alert: cost is ${{cost}}'). Available variables: automation_name, model, status, error_message, status_code, cost, latency, customer_identifier, prompt_name, severity. For aggregation output: <output_field_name> (e.g. cost_sum, error_count). Notification flattens the full namespace as template variables automatically.

WEBHOOK → webhook_url: str (required), webhook_secret: str (optional), is_including_scores: bool (optional), source: 'event' (default) | 'input' | 'state.<task_id>' (optional). Output: {webhook_url, dispatched: bool}.

AGGREGATION → time_step_minutes: int 1-10080 (default 5), metrics: [{field_name, aggregation_function: sum|avg|count|max|min, output_field_name (ALWAYS include — use field_function format, e.g. cost_sum, latency_avg; when omitted the output key auto-names <field_name>_<aggregation_function> — cost/avg → cost_avg, NEVER avg_cost), filters (optional per-metric pre-filter, applied per event before the metric increments)}].

Field names need the namespace dotpath prefix (event.*). WARNING: unlike condition and switch policies, metric filters are NOT validated at save time. A binary-expression object ({'left': ..., 'right': ..., 'operator': ...}) or any other wrong shape saves cleanly and then silently matches NOTHING at runtime, so the metric aggregates zero events and the downstream threshold never fires. Get the shape right on the first write.
For broad event filtering, use a condition task BEFORE aggregation. In type='monitors' automations, aggregation defaults is_comparing_to_previous=true (output includes % change vs the previous window; explicit false opts out; not defaulted when a metric uses max/min). Output: {aggregated_values: {<output_field_name>: value}, is_finished: {<field>: bool}}.

SWITCH → cases: array of case objects, each with EITHER {condition_id: '<uuid>', target: '<task_id>'} (saved condition) OR {condition_policy: {dotpath_field: {operator, value}}, target: '<task_id>'} (inline condition). First matching case wins. default: fallback target task id (optional). Switch evaluates against namespace (same dotpath rules as condition). Switch routes via case targets — does NOT need 'next' field.

COMPUTE → function: 'ratio'|'percentage'|'difference'|'weighted_average' (required), inputs: [{source: 'state.<task_id>', field: '<field_name>', weight: <float>}] (required). Binary functions (ratio, percentage, difference) take exactly 2 operands. weighted_average takes 2+ operands with weight field. label: optional human-readable name. Output: {result: <number>}.

GET_LOGS → window_seconds: int (required, ≤ 604800 = 7 days; fallback when no previous-fire anchor exists), metrics: array of DASHBOARD_METRICS names (required, e.g. number_of_requests, total_cost, total_tokens, error_count, error_percentage, average_cost, average_latency, average_ttft, unique_customers; max_tpm is rejected), group_by: array of bare CHLogV3 columns (organization_key_id, model, provider_id, environment, customer_identifier, prompt_id, status_code; empty = one summary row; a multi-element list is ONE composite grouping), breakdowns: array of column lists — independent per-dimension rollups, mutually exclusive with group_by (max 10), order_by: {field, direction} (optional, defaults first-metric desc), max_groups: int (default 100), include_prior_period: bool (adds prior-window totals for delta rendering). No custom metadata.X paths and no filtering — the slice is org + window.

GET_TRACES → trace-level sibling of get_logs over the trace agg table. window_seconds + metrics required; metrics from TRACE_METRICS (trace_count, total_cost, average_cost_per_trace, total_tokens, average_tokens_per_trace, error_count, average_duration, max_duration, average_spans_per_trace); group_by limited to organization_key_id, environment, customer_identifier (no model — a trace spans multiple models). No breakdowns / include_prior_period.

LIMIT_BREACHES → reports live limit-policy breaches at fire time (no window). scope: 'api_key' (only supported value, default), max_rows: int (default 50). Config may be empty {}.

GET_PULSE → pulls the report window's error-issue pulse facts for downstream summarization. max_issues: int (default 10), window_seconds: int (optional fallback when no previous-fire anchor — set to the same value as the report's get_logs tasks). Config may be empty {}.

Filterable fields and their semantics: "provider_id" — provider slug for provider-scoped questions. Canonical slugs: "anthropic", "openai", "azure_openai", "bedrock", "google_gemini_ai", "google_vertex_ai", "cohere", "deepseek", "fireworks", "groq", "mistral", "moonshot", "openrouter", "perplexity", "together_ai", "xai", "cerebras". REQUIRED when the user names a specific provider; without it the tool returns a global ranking/summary across ALL providers, which is the wrong answer for provider-scoped questions. If the user says "Google" without specifying Gemini vs Vertex, ask which one or call separately for both and combine. Example: {"provider_id": {"operator": "", "value": "anthropic"}}. "model" — specific model string; used for model-name filtering, NOT provider filtering. Use operator "icontains" for model — stored names carry version/date suffixes ("gpt-5.1-2025-11-13"), so an exact match on "gpt-5.1" misses most logs. "organization_key_id" — UUID of an API key (resolve a user-given key name via api_key_list first; this field never accepts names). "customer_identifier" — end-user/customer tag string. "deployment_name" — deployment slug string. tools.name: dashboard_metric_chart
tools.description: Get one metric over time as a chart. Response data is a chart payload — {"type": "chart", "series": [{"name": <series>, "points": [{"x": <ISO timestamp>, "y": <value|null>}]}]} — that the chat renders as a real chart. The numbers are already shown to the user: describe the trend, call out the peaks and gaps, and do NOT retype the values into your message. A null y is a bucket with no data, not a zero. Use metric to pick the series value: number_of_requests (default), total_cost (USD), average_cost (USD per request), total_tokens, average_tokens (per request), cache_hit_percentage (prompt cache hit rate, 0-100), error_count, error_percentage (error rate, 0-100), average_latency (seconds), average_ttft (seconds) or average_tps — one metric per call, so call again for another. This is the tool for any 'X over time' / 'X trend' question, errors and latency included — error_percentage is the metric for 'error rate as a trend'. Use breakdown_by to choose the series dimension: model (default), deployment_name, customer_identifier, or organization_key_id (per API key; series are keyed by key id with an id->name map attached). Use scope to choose the counted entity: span (default) counts individual spans/LLM requests; trace counts whole traces (a trace is failed when ANY of its spans failed — usually what 'how often do my runs fail' means; buckets key on trace start); thread counts threads by latest activity. Non-span scopes serve a subset: trace allows number_of_requests (=trace count), total_cost, total_tokens, error_count, error_percentage, average_cost, average_tokens, with breakdown_by limited to customer_identifier or organization_key_id (omit for one all-traces series); thread allows number_of_requests (=thread count), total_cost, total_tokens, average_latency, average_ttft, average_tps, with no breakdown_by. filters require scope=span. Long windows are downsampled and only the largest series are kept.

breakdown_by.description: Column to break down by (default: model).

scope.description: Entity the series counts (default: span). See the tool description for each scope's metric and breakdown subset.

metric.description: Metric charted on the y axis (default: number_of_requests).

type.description: Task type. get_logs/get_traces/limit_breaches/get_pulse/pulse_summarize are REPORT building blocks — use them in type='reports' evaluators with trigger_event_type='scheduled'.

label.description: Optional human-readable label for the task (e.g., 'Cost aggregation (5m)').

next.description: REQUIRED for task chaining. ID of the next task to execute after this one succeeds. Without 'next', the evaluator STOPS after this task (no sequential fallback). Example: if task A should flow to task B, set A's next to B's id.

config.description:
Task-specific configuration. Required fields per type:

NAMESPACE: Every task evaluates against a namespace with 4 keys: event (original log, flattened), input (previous task output), state (all upstream results keyed by task id/label), context (org/automation metadata). Condition/switch field names are dotpaths: 'event.status', 'state.<task_id>.cost_sum'. Simple field names do NOT work — always prefix with event./state.

CONDITION → condition_policy: {dotpath_field: {operator, value}} for inline rules. FIELD NAMES MUST use namespace dotpath prefix:
• Event fields: 'event.status', 'event.cost', 'event.model', 'event.latency', etc.
• Upstream task output: 'state.<task_id>.cost_sum', 'state.<task_id>.score', etc.
NEVER use 'input.<field>' in condition_policy — the frontend cannot render it. Always use 'state.<task_id>.<field>' to reference upstream task output. Policy keys ARE the dotpath field names — a binary-expression object ({'left': <field>, 'right': <value>, 'operator': <op>}) is rejected at save time.
OPERATOR RULES BY FIELD TYPE:
• Categorical (status, status_code, model, provider_id, log_type, deployment_name): ALWAYS 'in' with array: {"event.model": {"operator": "in", "value": ["gpt-4o"]}}. Exclude with 'not': {"event.status": {"operator": "not", "value": ["failed"]}}.
• Numeric (cost, latency, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_request_tokens): 'lte'/'gte'/'gt'/'lt' for ranges: {"event.cost": {"operator": "gte", "value": 0.01}}.
• Boolean (stream, cache_bit, has_tool_calls, is_root_span, positive_feedback): 'in' with array: {"event.stream": {"operator": "in", "value": [true]}}.
• Text (customer_identifier, thread_identifier, custom_identifier, group_identifier, prompt_id, prompt_name, span_name, span_workflow_name): 'icontains', 'startswith', 'in', 'not', 'empty', 'not_empty'.
NEVER use '' (empty string) or '=' as operator. Status values: 'failed' (errors), 'success', 'warning'. OR condition_id (str) for saved conditions. Also: on_true (default 'continue'), on_false (default 'stop').
Output: {triggered: bool, triggered_metrics: [...]}.

SAMPLING → rate: float 0.0-1.0 (e.g., 0.1 = 10% of events). Output: passthrough (input forwarded to next task).

EVAL → evaluator_id: str (UUID from evaluator_list). Output: {score, evaluator_name, ...} (evaluation results).

INGEST → target_type: 'dataset'|'log'|'experiment', target: {dataset_id: '<uuid>'} or {experiment_id: '<uuid>'} or {} (for log), source: 'event' (default) | 'input' | 'state.<task_id>'. Output: confirmation with ingested ID.

NOTIFICATION → notification_method_id: str (UUID from notification_method_list), severity: 'low'|'medium'|'high'|'urgent', message_template: str with LITERAL double-brace Jinja2 placeholders (you MUST wrap each variable name in double curly braces — e.g. '{{automation_name}} alert: cost is ${{cost}}'). Available variables: automation_name, model, status, error_message, status_code, cost, latency, customer_identifier, prompt_name, severity. For aggregation output: <output_field_name> (e.g. cost_sum, error_count). Notification flattens the full namespace as template variables automatically.
Output: {dispatch_results, notifications_sent}.

WEBHOOK → webhook_url: str (required), webhook_secret: str (optional), is_including_scores: bool (optional), source: 'event' (default) | 'input' | 'state.<task_id>' (optional). Output: {webhook_url, dispatched: bool}.

AGGREGATION → time_step_minutes: int 1-10080 (default 5), metrics: [{field_name, aggregation_function: sum|avg|count|max|min, output_field_name (ALWAYS include — use field_function format, e.g. cost_sum, latency_avg; when omitted the output key auto-names <field_name>_<aggregation_function> — cost/avg → cost_avg, NEVER avg_cost), filters (optional per-metric pre-filter, applied per event before the metric increments)}].
AGGREGATION metric filters use the SAME shape as condition_policy above — {dotpath_field: {operator, value}}, e.g. {"event.status": {"operator": "in", "value": ["failed"]}} — and the SAME operator rules by field type: categorical and boolean take 'in'/'not' with an ARRAY value, numeric take 'gte'/'lte'/'gt'/'lt', text takes 'icontains'/'startswith'/'in'/'not'/'empty'/'not_empty'. Field names need the namespace dotpath prefix (event.*). WARNING: unlike condition and switch policies, metric filters are NOT validated at save time. A binary-expression object ({'left': ..., 'right': ..., 'operator': ...}) or any other wrong shape saves cleanly and then silently matches NOTHING at runtime, so the metric aggregates zero events and the downstream threshold never fires. Get the shape right on the first write.
For broad event filtering, use a condition task BEFORE aggregation. In type='monitors' evaluators, aggregation defaults is_comparing_to_previous=true (output includes % change vs the previous window; explicit false opts out; not defaulted when a metric uses max/min). Output: {aggregated_values: {<output_field_name>: value}, is_finished: {<field>: bool}}.

SWITCH → cases: array of case objects, each with EITHER {condition_id: '<uuid>', target: '<task_id>'} (saved condition) OR {condition_policy: {dotpath_field: {operator, value}}, target: '<task_id>'} (inline condition). First matching case wins. default: fallback target task id (optional). Switch evaluates against namespace (same dotpath rules as condition). Switch routes via case targets — does NOT need 'next' field.

COMPUTE → function: 'ratio'|'percentage'|'difference'|'weighted_average' (required), inputs: [{source: 'state.<task_id>', field: '<field_name>', weight: <float>}] (required). Binary functions (ratio, percentage, difference) take exactly 2 operands. weighted_average takes 2+ operands with weight field. label: optional human-readable name. Output: {result: <number>}.

PROMPT → prompt_id: str (UUID from prompt_list — NEVER pass a prompt name like 'Math Tutor' as prompt_id; call prompt_list first and use the returned id field), version: int (optional), override_params: object (optional model/temperature/max_tokens overrides). Loads the prompt template, renders variables from the input namespace, and runs an LLM completion. Output: {input, output, metrics: {cost, latency, tokens}}.

COMPLETION → model: str (LLM name, required, e.g. 'gpt-4o-mini'), temperature/max_tokens/top_p (optional). Sends input messages directly to the LLM without a template. Output: {input, output, metrics: {cost, latency, tokens}}.

THROTTLE → cooldown_seconds: int 1-86400 (required). Fires once per cooldown window and suppresses subsequent firings until the window elapses. Typical placement: after a threshold condition, before a notification/webhook, to prevent alert spam.

REPORT TASKS (type='reports' + trigger_event_type='scheduled' only; the digest window is anchored to the span since the previous scheduled fire):

GET_LOGS → window_seconds: int (required, ≤ 604800 = 7 days; fallback when no previous-fire anchor exists), metrics: array of DASHBOARD_METRICS names (required, e.g. number_of_requests, total_cost, total_tokens, error_count, error_percentage, average_cost, average_latency, average_ttft, unique_customers; max_tpm is rejected), group_by: array of bare CHLogV3 columns (organization_key_id, model, provider_id, environment, customer_identifier, prompt_id, status_code; empty = one summary row; a multi-element list is ONE composite grouping), breakdowns: array of column lists — independent per-dimension rollups, mutually exclusive with group_by (max 10), order_by: {field, direction} (optional, defaults first-metric desc), max_groups: int (default 100), include_prior_period: bool (adds prior-window totals for delta rendering). No custom metadata.X paths and no filtering — the slice is org + window.

GET_TRACES → trace-level sibling of get_logs over the trace agg table. window_seconds + metrics required; metrics from TRACE_METRICS (trace_count, total_cost, average_cost_per_trace, total_tokens, average_tokens_per_trace, error_count, average_duration, max_duration, average_spans_per_trace); group_by limited to organization_key_id, environment, customer_identifier (no model — a trace spans multiple models). No breakdowns / include_prior_period.

LIMIT_BREACHES → reports live limit-policy breaches at fire time (no window). scope: 'api_key' (only supported value, default), max_rows: int (default 50). Config may be empty {}.

GET_PULSE → pulls the report window's error-issue pulse facts for downstream summarization. max_issues: int (default 10), window_seconds: int (optional fallback when no previous-fire anchor — set to the same value as the report's get_logs tasks). Config may be empty {}.

PULSE_SUMMARIZE → LLM summary of upstream get_pulse facts. No config knobs — pass config {} and chain it directly after a get_pulse task.

type.description: Task type. get_logs/get_traces/limit_breaches/get_pulse/pulse_summarize are REPORT building blocks — use them in type='reports' monitors with trigger_event_type='scheduled'.

label.description: Optional human-readable label for the task (e.g., 'Cost aggregation (5m)').

next.description: REQUIRED for task chaining. ID of the next task to execute after this one succeeds. Without 'next', the monitor STOPS after this task (no sequential fallback). Example: if task A should flow to task B, set A's next to B's id.

config.description:
Task-specific configuration. Required fields per type:

NAMESPACE: Every task evaluates against a namespace with 4 keys: event (original log, flattened), input (previous task output), state (all upstream results keyed by task id/label), context (org/automation metadata). Condition/switch field names are dotpaths: 'event.status', 'state.<task_id>.cost_sum'. Simple field names do NOT work — always prefix with event./state.

CONDITION → condition_policy: {dotpath_field: {operator, value}} for inline rules. FIELD NAMES MUST use namespace dotpath prefix:
• Event fields: 'event.status', 'event.cost', 'event.model', 'event.latency', etc.
• Upstream task output: 'state.<task_id>.cost_sum', 'state.<task_id>.score', etc.
NEVER use 'input.<field>' in condition_policy — the frontend cannot render it. Always use 'state.<task_id>.<field>' to reference upstream task output. Policy keys ARE the dotpath field names — a binary-expression object ({'left': <field>, 'right': <value>, 'operator': <op>}) is rejected at save time.
OPERATOR RULES BY FIELD TYPE:
• Categorical (status, status_code, model, provider_id, log_type, deployment_name): ALWAYS 'in' with array: {"event.model": {"operator": "in", "value": ["gpt-4o"]}}. Exclude with 'not': {"event.status": {"operator": "not", "value": ["failed"]}}.
• Numeric (cost, latency, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_request_tokens): 'lte'/'gte'/'gt'/'lt' for ranges: {"event.cost": {"operator": "gte", "value": 0.01}}.
• Boolean (stream, cache_bit, has_tool_calls, is_root_span, positive_feedback): 'in' with array: {"event.stream": {"operator": "in", "value": [true]}}.
• Text (customer_identifier, thread_identifier, custom_identifier, group_identifier, prompt_id, prompt_name, span_name, span_workflow_name): 'icontains', 'startswith', 'in', 'not', 'empty', 'not_empty'.
NEVER use '' (empty string) or '=' as operator. Status values: 'failed' (errors), 'success', 'warning'. OR condition_id (str) for saved conditions. Also: on_true (default 'continue'), on_false (default 'stop').
Output: {triggered: bool, triggered_metrics: [...]}.

SAMPLING → rate: float 0.0-1.0 (e.g., 0.1 = 10% of events). Output: passthrough (input forwarded to next task).

EVAL → evaluator_id: str (UUID from evaluator_list). Output: {score, evaluator_name, ...} (evaluation results).

INGEST → target_type: 'dataset'|'log'|'experiment', target: {dataset_id: '<uuid>'} or {experiment_id: '<uuid>'} or {} (for log), source: 'event' (default) | 'input' | 'state.<task_id>'. Output: confirmation with ingested ID.

NOTIFICATION → notification_method_id: str (UUID from notification_method_list), severity: 'low'|'medium'|'high'|'urgent', message_template: str with LITERAL double-brace Jinja2 placeholders (you MUST wrap each variable name in double curly braces — e.g. '{{automation_name}} alert: cost is ${{cost}}'). Available variables: automation_name, model, status, error_message, status_code, cost, latency, customer_identifier, prompt_name, severity. For aggregation output: <output_field_name> (e.g. cost_sum, error_count). Notification flattens the full namespace as template variables automatically.
Output: {dispatch_results, notifications_sent}.

WEBHOOK → webhook_url: str (required), webhook_secret: str (optional), is_including_scores: bool (optional), source: 'event' (default) | 'input' | 'state.<task_id>' (optional). Output: {webhook_url, dispatched: bool}.

AGGREGATION → time_step_minutes: int 1-10080 (default 5), metrics: [{field_name, aggregation_function: sum|avg|count|max|min, output_field_name (ALWAYS include — use field_function format, e.g. cost_sum, latency_avg; when omitted the output key auto-names <field_name>_<aggregation_function> — cost/avg → cost_avg, NEVER avg_cost), filters (optional per-metric pre-filter, applied per event before the metric increments)}].
AGGREGATION metric filters use the SAME shape as condition_policy above — {dotpath_field: {operator, value}}, e.g. {"event.status": {"operator": "in", "value": ["failed"]}} — and the SAME operator rules by field type: categorical and boolean take 'in'/'not' with an ARRAY value, numeric take 'gte'/'lte'/'gt'/'lt', text takes 'icontains'/'startswith'/'in'/'not'/'empty'/'not_empty'. Field names need the namespace dotpath prefix (event.*). WARNING: unlike condition and switch policies, metric filters are NOT validated at save time. A binary-expression object ({'left': ..., 'right': ..., 'operator': ...}) or any other wrong shape saves cleanly and then silently matches NOTHING at runtime, so the metric aggregates zero events and the downstream threshold never fires. Get the shape right on the first write.
For broad event filtering, use a condition task BEFORE aggregation. In type='monitors' monitors, aggregation defaults is_comparing_to_previous=true (output includes % change vs the previous window; explicit false opts out; not defaulted when a metric uses max/min). Output: {aggregated_values: {<output_field_name>: value}, is_finished: {<field>: bool}}.

SWITCH → cases: array of case objects, each with EITHER {condition_id: '<uuid>', target: '<task_id>'} (saved condition) OR {condition_policy: {dotpath_field: {operator, value}}, target: '<task_id>'} (inline condition). First matching case wins. default: fallback target task id (optional). Switch evaluates against namespace (same dotpath rules as condition). Switch routes via case targets — does NOT need 'next' field.

COMPUTE → function: 'ratio'|'percentage'|'difference'|'weighted_average' (required), inputs: [{source: 'state.<task_id>', field: '<field_name>', weight: <float>}] (required). Binary functions (ratio, percentage, difference) take exactly 2 operands. weighted_average takes 2+ operands with weight field. label: optional human-readable name. Output: {result: <number>}.

PROMPT → prompt_id: str (UUID from prompt_list — NEVER pass a prompt name like 'Math Tutor' as prompt_id; call prompt_list first and use the returned id field), version: int (optional), override_params: object (optional model/temperature/max_tokens overrides). Loads the prompt template, renders variables from the input namespace, and runs an LLM completion. Output: {input, output, metrics: {cost, latency, tokens}}.

COMPLETION → model: str (LLM name, required, e.g. 'gpt-4o-mini'), temperature/max_tokens/top_p (optional). Sends input messages directly to the LLM without a template. Output: {input, output, metrics: {cost, latency, tokens}}.

THROTTLE → cooldown_seconds: int 1-86400 (required). Fires once per cooldown window and suppresses subsequent firings until the window elapses. Typical placement: after a threshold condition, before a notification/webhook, to prevent alert spam.

REPORT TASKS (type='reports' + trigger_event_type='scheduled' only; the digest window is anchored to the span since the previous scheduled fire):

GET_LOGS → window_seconds: int (required, ≤ 604800 = 7 days; fallback when no previous-fire anchor exists), metrics: array of DASHBOARD_METRICS names (required, e.g. number_of_requests, total_cost, total_tokens, error_count, error_percentage, average_cost, average_latency, average_ttft, unique_customers; max_tpm is rejected), group_by: array of bare CHLogV3 columns (organization_key_id, model, provider_id, environment, customer_identifier, prompt_id, status_code; empty = one summary row; a multi-element list is ONE composite grouping), breakdowns: array of column lists — independent per-dimension rollups, mutually exclusive with group_by (max 10), order_by: {field, direction} (optional, defaults first-metric desc), max_groups: int (default 100), include_prior_period: bool (adds prior-window totals for delta rendering). No custom metadata.X paths and no filtering — the slice is org + window.

GET_TRACES → trace-level sibling of get_logs over the trace agg table. window_seconds + metrics required; metrics from TRACE_METRICS (trace_count, total_cost, average_cost_per_trace, total_tokens, average_tokens_per_trace, error_count, average_duration, max_duration, average_spans_per_trace); group_by limited to organization_key_id, environment, customer_identifier (no model — a trace spans multiple models). No breakdowns / include_prior_period.

LIMIT_BREACHES → reports live limit-policy breaches at fire time (no window). scope: 'api_key' (only supported value, default), max_rows: int (default 50). Config may be empty {}.

GET_PULSE → pulls the report window's error-issue pulse facts for downstream summarization. max_issues: int (default 10), window_seconds: int (optional fallback when no previous-fire anchor — set to the same value as the report's get_logs tasks). Config may be empty {}.

PULSE_SUMMARIZE → LLM summary of upstream get_pulse facts. No config knobs — pass config {} and chain it directly after a get_pulse task.

config.description:
Task-specific configuration. Required fields per type:

NAMESPACE: Every task evaluates against a namespace with 4 keys: event (original log, flattened), input (previous task output), state (all upstream results keyed by task id/label), context (org/automation metadata). Condition/switch field names are dotpaths: 'event.status', 'state.<task_id>.cost_sum'. Simple field names do NOT work — always prefix with event./state.

CONDITION → condition_policy: {dotpath_field: {operator, value}} for inline rules. FIELD NAMES MUST use namespace dotpath prefix:
• Event fields: 'event.status', 'event.cost', 'event.model', 'event.latency', etc.
• Upstream task output: 'state.<task_id>.cost_sum', 'state.<task_id>.score', etc.
NEVER use 'input.<field>' in condition_policy — the frontend cannot render it. Always use 'state.<task_id>.<field>' to reference upstream task output. Policy keys ARE the dotpath field names — a binary-expression object ({'left': <field>, 'right': <value>, 'operator': <op>}) is rejected at save time.
OPERATOR RULES BY FIELD TYPE:
• Categorical (status, status_code, model, provider_id, log_type, deployment_name): ALWAYS 'in' with array: {"event.model": {"operator": "in", "value": ["gpt-4o"]}}. Exclude with 'not': {"event.status": {"operator": "not", "value": ["failed"]}}.
• Numeric (cost, latency, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_request_tokens): 'lte'/'gte'/'gt'/'lt' for ranges: {"event.cost": {"operator": "gte", "value": 0.01}}.
• Boolean (stream, cache_bit, has_tool_calls, is_root_span, positive_feedback): 'in' with array: {"event.stream": {"operator": "in", "value": [true]}}.
• Text (customer_identifier, thread_identifier, custom_identifier, group_identifier, prompt_id, prompt_name, span_name, span_workflow_name): 'icontains', 'startswith', 'in', 'not', 'empty', 'not_empty'.
NEVER use '' (empty string) or '=' as operator. Status values: 'failed' (errors), 'success', 'warning'. OR condition_id (str) for saved conditions. Also: on_true (default 'continue'), on_false (default 'stop').
Output: {triggered: bool, triggered_metrics: [...]}.

SAMPLING → rate: float 0.0-1.0 (e.g., 0.1 = 10% of events). Output: passthrough (input forwarded to next task).

EVAL → evaluator_id: str (UUID from evaluator_list). Output: {score, evaluator_name, ...} (evaluation results).

INGEST → target_type: 'dataset'|'log'|'experiment', target: {dataset_id: '<uuid>'} or {experiment_id: '<uuid>'} or {} (for log), source: 'event' (default) | 'input' | 'state.<task_id>'. Output: confirmation with ingested ID.

NOTIFICATION → notification_method_id: str (UUID from notification_method_list), severity: 'low'|'medium'|'high'|'urgent', message_template: str with LITERAL double-brace Jinja2 placeholders (you MUST wrap each variable name in double curly braces — e.g. '{{automation_name}} alert: cost is ${{cost}}'). Available variables: automation_name, model, status, error_message, status_code, cost, latency, customer_identifier, prompt_name, severity. For aggregation output: <output_field_name> (e.g. cost_sum, error_count). Notification flattens the full namespace as template variables automatically.
Output: {dispatch_results, notifications_sent}.

WEBHOOK → webhook_url: str (required), webhook_secret: str (optional), is_including_scores: bool (optional), source: 'event' (default) | 'input' | 'state.<task_id>' (optional). Output: {webhook_url, dispatched: bool}.

AGGREGATION → time_step_minutes: int 1-10080 (default 5), metrics: [{field_name, aggregation_function: sum|avg|count|max|min, output_field_name (ALWAYS include — use field_function format, e.g. cost_sum, latency_avg; when omitted the output key auto-names <field_name>_<aggregation_function> — cost/avg → cost_avg, NEVER avg_cost), filters (optional per-metric pre-filter, applied per event before the metric increments)}].
AGGREGATION metric filters use the SAME shape as condition_policy above — {dotpath_field: {operator, value}}, e.g. {"event.status": {"operator": "in", "value": ["failed"]}} — and the SAME operator rules by field type: categorical and boolean take 'in'/'not' with an ARRAY value, numeric take 'gte'/'lte'/'gt'/'lt', text takes 'icontains'/'startswith'/'in'/'not'/'empty'/'not_empty'. Field names need the namespace dotpath prefix (event.*). WARNING: unlike condition and switch policies, metric filters are NOT validated at save time. A binary-expression object ({'left': ..., 'right': ..., 'operator': ...}) or any other wrong shape saves cleanly and then silently matches NOTHING at runtime, so the metric aggregates zero events and the downstream threshold never fires. Get the shape right on the first write.
For broad event filtering, use a condition task BEFORE aggregation. In type='monitors' monitors, aggregation defaults is_comparing_to_previous=true (output includes % change vs the previous window; explicit false opts out; not defaulted when a metric uses max/min). Output: {aggregated_values: {<output_field_name>: value}, is_finished: {<field>: bool}}.

SWITCH → cases: array of case objects, each with EITHER {condition_id: '<uuid>', target: '<task_id>'} (saved condition) OR {condition_policy: {dotpath_field: {operator, value}}, target: '<task_id>'} (inline condition). First matching case wins. default: fallback target task id (optional). Switch evaluates against namespace (same dotpath rules as condition). Switch routes via case targets — does NOT need 'next' field.

COMPUTE → function: 'ratio'|'percentage'|'difference'|'weighted_average' (required), inputs: [{source: 'state.<task_id>', field: '<field_name>', weight: <float>}] (required). Binary functions (ratio, percentage, difference) take exactly 2 operands. weighted_average takes 2+ operands with weight field. label: optional human-readable name. Output: {result: <number>}.

PROMPT → prompt_id: str (UUID from prompt_list — NEVER pass a prompt name like 'Math Tutor' as prompt_id; call prompt_list first and use the returned id field), version: int (optional), override_params: object (optional model/temperature/max_tokens overrides). Loads the prompt template, renders variables from the input namespace, and runs an LLM completion. Output: {input, output, metrics: {cost, latency, tokens}}.

COMPLETION → model: str (LLM name, required, e.g. 'gpt-4o-mini'), temperature/max_tokens/top_p (optional). Sends input messages directly to the LLM without a template. Output: {input, output, metrics: {cost, latency, tokens}}.

THROTTLE → cooldown_seconds: int 1-86400 (required). Fires once per cooldown window and suppresses subsequent firings until the window elapses. Typical placement: after a threshold condition, before a notification/webhook, to prevent alert spam.

REPORT TASKS (type='reports' + trigger_event_type='scheduled' only; the digest window is anchored to the span since the previous scheduled fire):

GET_LOGS → window_seconds: int (required, ≤ 604800 = 7 days; fallback when no previous-fire anchor exists), metrics: array of DASHBOARD_METRICS names (required, e.g. number_of_requests, total_cost, total_tokens, error_count, error_percentage, average_cost, average_latency, average_ttft, unique_customers; max_tpm is rejected), group_by: array of bare CHLogV3 columns (organization_key_id, model, provider_id, environment, customer_identifier, prompt_id, status_code; empty = one summary row; a multi-element list is ONE composite grouping), breakdowns: array of column lists — independent per-dimension rollups, mutually exclusive with group_by (max 10), order_by: {field, direction} (optional, defaults first-metric desc), max_groups: int (default 100), include_prior_period: bool (adds prior-window totals for delta rendering). No custom metadata.X paths and no filtering — the slice is org + window.

GET_TRACES → trace-level sibling of get_logs over the trace agg table. window_seconds + metrics required; metrics from TRACE_METRICS (trace_count, total_cost, average_cost_per_trace, total_tokens, average_tokens_per_trace, error_count, average_duration, max_duration, average_spans_per_trace); group_by limited to organization_key_id, environment, customer_identifier (no model — a trace spans multiple models). No breakdowns / include_prior_period.

LIMIT_BREACHES → reports live limit-policy breaches at fire time (no window). scope: 'api_key' (only supported value, default), max_rows: int (default 50). Config may be empty {}.

GET_PULSE → pulls the report window's error-issue pulse facts for downstream summarization. max_issues: int (default 10), window_seconds: int (optional fallback when no previous-fire anchor — set to the same value as the report's get_logs tasks). Config may be empty {}.

PULSE_SUMMARIZE → LLM summary of upstream get_pulse facts. No config knobs — pass config {} and chain it directly after a get_pulse task.

config.description:
Task-specific configuration. Required fields per type:

NAMESPACE: Every task evaluates against a namespace with 4 keys: event (original log, flattened), input (previous task output), state (all upstream results keyed by task id/label), context (org/automation metadata). Condition/switch field names are dotpaths: 'event.status', 'state.<task_id>.cost_sum'. Simple field names do NOT work — always prefix with event./state.

CONDITION → condition_policy: {dotpath_field: {operator, value}} for inline rules. FIELD NAMES MUST use namespace dotpath prefix:
• Event fields: 'event.status', 'event.cost', 'event.model', 'event.latency', etc.
• Upstream task output: 'state.<task_id>.cost_sum', 'state.<task_id>.score', etc.
NEVER use 'input.<field>' in condition_policy — the frontend cannot render it. Always use 'state.<task_id>.<field>' to reference upstream task output. Policy keys ARE the dotpath field names — a binary-expression object ({'left': <field>, 'right': <value>, 'operator': <op>}) is rejected at save time.
OPERATOR RULES BY FIELD TYPE:
• Categorical (status, status_code, model, provider_id, log_type, deployment_name): ALWAYS 'in' with array: {"event.model": {"operator": "in", "value": ["gpt-4o"]}}. Exclude with 'not': {"event.status": {"operator": "not", "value": ["failed"]}}.
• Numeric (cost, latency, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_request_tokens): 'lte'/'gte'/'gt'/'lt' for ranges: {"event.cost": {"operator": "gte", "value": 0.01}}.
• Boolean (stream, cache_bit, has_tool_calls, is_root_span, positive_feedback): 'in' with array: {"event.stream": {"operator": "in", "value": [true]}}.
• Text (customer_identifier, thread_identifier, custom_identifier, group_identifier, prompt_id, prompt_name, span_name, span_workflow_name): 'icontains', 'startswith', 'in', 'not', 'empty', 'not_empty'.
NEVER use '' (empty string) or '=' as operator. Status values: 'failed' (errors), 'success', 'warning'. OR condition_id (str) for saved conditions. Also: on_true (default 'continue'), on_false (default 'stop').
Output: {triggered: bool, triggered_metrics: [...]}.

SAMPLING → rate: float 0.0-1.0 (e.g., 0.1 = 10% of events). Output: passthrough (input forwarded to next task).

EVAL → evaluator_id: str (UUID from evaluator_list). Output: {score, evaluator_name, ...} (evaluation results).

INGEST → target_type: 'dataset'|'log'|'experiment', target: {dataset_id: '<uuid>'} or {experiment_id: '<uuid>'} or {} (for log), source: 'event' (default) | 'input' | 'state.<task_id>'. Output: confirmation with ingested ID.

NOTIFICATION → notification_method_id: str (UUID from notification_method_list), severity: 'low'|'medium'|'high'|'urgent', message_template: str with LITERAL double-brace Jinja2 placeholders (you MUST wrap each variable name in double curly braces — e.g. '{{automation_name}} alert: cost is ${{cost}}'). Available variables: automation_name, model, status, error_message, status_code, cost, latency, customer_identifier, prompt_name, severity. For aggregation output: <output_field_name> (e.g. cost_sum, error_count). Notification flattens the full namespace as template variables automatically.
Output: {dispatch_results, notifications_sent}.

WEBHOOK → webhook_url: str (required), webhook_secret: str (optional), is_including_scores: bool (optional), source: 'event' (default) | 'input' | 'state.<task_id>' (optional). Output: {webhook_url, dispatched: bool}.

AGGREGATION → time_step_minutes: int 1-10080 (default 5), metrics: [{field_name, aggregation_function: sum|avg|count|max|min, output_field_name (ALWAYS include — use field_function format, e.g. cost_sum, latency_avg; when omitted the output key auto-names <field_name>_<aggregation_function> — cost/avg → cost_avg, NEVER avg_cost), filters (optional per-metric pre-filter, applied per event before the metric increments)}].
AGGREGATION metric filters use the SAME shape as condition_policy above — {dotpath_field: {operator, value}}, e.g. {"event.status": {"operator": "in", "value": ["failed"]}} — and the SAME operator rules by field type: categorical and boolean take 'in'/'not' with an ARRAY value, numeric take 'gte'/'lte'/'gt'/'lt', text takes 'icontains'/'startswith'/'in'/'not'/'empty'/'not_empty'. Field names need the namespace dotpath prefix (event.*). WARNING: unlike condition and switch policies, metric filters are NOT validated at save time. A binary-expression object ({'left': ..., 'right': ..., 'operator': ...}) or any other wrong shape saves cleanly and then silently matches NOTHING at runtime, so the metric aggregates zero events and the downstream threshold never fires. Get the shape right on the first write.
For broad event filtering, use a condition task BEFORE aggregation. In type='monitors' reports, aggregation defaults is_comparing_to_previous=true (output includes % change vs the previous window; explicit false opts out; not defaulted when a metric uses max/min). Output: {aggregated_values: {<output_field_name>: value}, is_finished: {<field>: bool}}.

SWITCH → cases: array of case objects, each with EITHER {condition_id: '<uuid>', target: '<task_id>'} (saved condition) OR {condition_policy: {dotpath_field: {operator, value}}, target: '<task_id>'} (inline condition). First matching case wins. default: fallback target task id (optional). Switch evaluates against namespace (same dotpath rules as condition). Switch routes via case targets — does NOT need 'next' field.

COMPUTE → function: 'ratio'|'percentage'|'difference'|'weighted_average' (required), inputs: [{source: 'state.<task_id>', field: '<field_name>', weight: <float>}] (required). Binary functions (ratio, percentage, difference) take exactly 2 operands. weighted_average takes 2+ operands with weight field. label: optional human-readable name. Output: {result: <number>}.

PROMPT → prompt_id: str (UUID from prompt_list — NEVER pass a prompt name like 'Math Tutor' as prompt_id; call prompt_list first and use the returned id field), version: int (optional), override_params: object (optional model/temperature/max_tokens overrides). Loads the prompt template, renders variables from the input namespace, and runs an LLM completion. Output: {input, output, metrics: {cost, latency, tokens}}.

COMPLETION → model: str (LLM name, required, e.g. 'gpt-4o-mini'), temperature/max_tokens/top_p (optional). Sends input messages directly to the LLM without a template. Output: {input, output, metrics: {cost, latency, tokens}}.

THROTTLE → cooldown_seconds: int 1-86400 (required). Fires once per cooldown window and suppresses subsequent firings until the window elapses. Typical placement: after a threshold condition, before a notification/webhook, to prevent alert spam.

REPORT TASKS (type='reports' + trigger_event_type='scheduled' only; the digest window is anchored to the span since the previous scheduled fire):

GET_LOGS → window_seconds: int (required, ≤ 604800 = 7 days; fallback when no previous-fire anchor exists), metrics: array of DASHBOARD_METRICS names (required, e.g. number_of_requests, total_cost, total_tokens, error_count, error_percentage, average_cost, average_latency, average_ttft, unique_customers; max_tpm is rejected), group_by: array of bare CHLogV3 columns (organization_key_id, model, provider_id, environment, customer_identifier, prompt_id, status_code; empty = one summary row; a multi-element list is ONE composite grouping), breakdowns: array of column lists — independent per-dimension rollups, mutually exclusive with group_by (max 10), order_by: {field, direction} (optional, defaults first-metric desc), max_groups: int (default 100), include_prior_period: bool (adds prior-window totals for delta rendering). No custom metadata.X paths and no filtering — the slice is org + window.

GET_TRACES → trace-level sibling of get_logs over the trace agg table. window_seconds + metrics required; metrics from TRACE_METRICS (trace_count, total_cost, average_cost_per_trace, total_tokens, average_tokens_per_trace, error_count, average_duration, max_duration, average_spans_per_trace); group_by limited to organization_key_id, environment, customer_identifier (no model — a trace spans multiple models). No breakdowns / include_prior_period.

LIMIT_BREACHES → reports live limit-policy breaches at fire time (no window). scope: 'api_key' (only supported value, default), max_rows: int (default 50). Config may be empty {}.

GET_PULSE → pulls the report window's error-issue pulse facts for downstream summarization. max_issues: int (default 10), window_seconds: int (optional fallback when no previous-fire anchor — set to the same value as the report's get_logs tasks). Config may be empty {}.

PULSE_SUMMARIZE → LLM summary of upstream get_pulse facts. No config knobs — pass config {} and chain it directly after a get_pulse task.

config.description:
Task-specific configuration. Required fields per type:

NAMESPACE: Every task evaluates against a namespace with 4 keys: event (original log, flattened), input (previous task output), state (all upstream results keyed by task id/label), context (org/automation metadata). Condition/switch field names are dotpaths: 'event.status', 'state.<task_id>.cost_sum'. Simple field names do NOT work — always prefix with event./state.

CONDITION → condition_policy: {dotpath_field: {operator, value}} for inline rules. FIELD NAMES MUST use namespace dotpath prefix:
• Event fields: 'event.status', 'event.cost', 'event.model', 'event.latency', etc.
• Upstream task output: 'state.<task_id>.cost_sum', 'state.<task_id>.score', etc.
NEVER use 'input.<field>' in condition_policy — the frontend cannot render it. Always use 'state.<task_id>.<field>' to reference upstream task output. Policy keys ARE the dotpath field names — a binary-expression object ({'left': <field>, 'right': <value>, 'operator': <op>}) is rejected at save time.
OPERATOR RULES BY FIELD TYPE:
• Categorical (status, status_code, model, provider_id, log_type, deployment_name): ALWAYS 'in' with array: {"event.model": {"operator": "in", "value": ["gpt-4o"]}}. Exclude with 'not': {"event.status": {"operator": "not", "value": ["failed"]}}.
• Numeric (cost, latency, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_request_tokens): 'lte'/'gte'/'gt'/'lt' for ranges: {"event.cost": {"operator": "gte", "value": 0.01}}.
• Boolean (stream, cache_bit, has_tool_calls, is_root_span, positive_feedback): 'in' with array: {"event.stream": {"operator": "in", "value": [true]}}.
• Text (customer_identifier, thread_identifier, custom_identifier, group_identifier, prompt_id, prompt_name, span_name, span_workflow_name): 'icontains', 'startswith', 'in', 'not', 'empty', 'not_empty'.
NEVER use '' (empty string) or '=' as operator. Status values: 'failed' (errors), 'success', 'warning'. OR condition_id (str) for saved conditions. Also: on_true (default 'continue'), on_false (default 'stop').
Output: {triggered: bool, triggered_metrics: [...]}.

SAMPLING → rate: float 0.0-1.0 (e.g., 0.1 = 10% of events). Output: passthrough (input forwarded to next task).

EVAL → evaluator_id: str (UUID from evaluator_list). Output: {score, evaluator_name, ...} (evaluation results).

INGEST → target_type: 'dataset'|'log'|'experiment', target: {dataset_id: '<uuid>'} or {experiment_id: '<uuid>'} or {} (for log), source: 'event' (default) | 'input' | 'state.<task_id>'. Output: confirmation with ingested ID.

NOTIFICATION → notification_method_id: str (UUID from notification_method_list), severity: 'low'|'medium'|'high'|'urgent', message_template: str with LITERAL double-brace Jinja2 placeholders (you MUST wrap each variable name in double curly braces — e.g. '{{automation_name}} alert: cost is ${{cost}}'). Available variables: automation_name, model, status, error_message, status_code, cost, latency, customer_identifier, prompt_name, severity. For aggregation output: <output_field_name> (e.g. cost_sum, error_count). Notification flattens the full namespace as template variables automatically.
Output: {dispatch_results, notifications_sent}.

WEBHOOK → webhook_url: str (required), webhook_secret: str (optional), is_including_scores: bool (optional), source: 'event' (default) | 'input' | 'state.<task_id>' (optional). Output: {webhook_url, dispatched: bool}.

AGGREGATION → time_step_minutes: int 1-10080 (default 5), metrics: [{field_name, aggregation_function: sum|avg|count|max|min, output_field_name (ALWAYS include — use field_function format, e.g. cost_sum, latency_avg; when omitted the output key auto-names <field_name>_<aggregation_function> — cost/avg → cost_avg, NEVER avg_cost), filters (optional per-metric pre-filter, applied per event before the metric increments)}].
AGGREGATION metric filters use the SAME shape as condition_policy above — {dotpath_field: {operator, value}}, e.g. {"event.status": {"operator": "in", "value": ["failed"]}} — and the SAME operator rules by field type: categorical and boolean take 'in'/'not' with an ARRAY value, numeric take 'gte'/'lte'/'gt'/'lt', text takes 'icontains'/'startswith'/'in'/'not'/'empty'/'not_empty'. Field names need the namespace dotpath prefix (event.*). WARNING: unlike condition and switch policies, metric filters are NOT validated at save time. A binary-expression object ({'left': ..., 'right': ..., 'operator': ...}) or any other wrong shape saves cleanly and then silently matches NOTHING at runtime, so the metric aggregates zero events and the downstream threshold never fires. Get the shape right on the first write.
For broad event filtering, use a condition task BEFORE aggregation. In type='monitors' reports, aggregation defaults is_comparing_to_previous=true (output includes % change vs the previous window; explicit false opts out; not defaulted when a metric uses max/min). Output: {aggregated_values: {<output_field_name>: value}, is_finished: {<field>: bool}}.

SWITCH → cases: array of case objects, each with EITHER {condition_id: '<uuid>', target: '<task_id>'} (saved condition) OR {condition_policy: {dotpath_field: {operator, value}}, target: '<task_id>'} (inline condition). First matching case wins. default: fallback target task id (optional). Switch evaluates against namespace (same dotpath rules as condition). Switch routes via case targets — does NOT need 'next' field.

COMPUTE → function: 'ratio'|'percentage'|'difference'|'weighted_average' (required), inputs: [{source: 'state.<task_id>', field: '<field_name>', weight: <float>}] (required). Binary functions (ratio, percentage, difference) take exactly 2 operands. weighted_average takes 2+ operands with weight field. label: optional human-readable name. Output: {result: <number>}.

PROMPT → prompt_id: str (UUID from prompt_list — NEVER pass a prompt name like 'Math Tutor' as prompt_id; call prompt_list first and use the returned id field), version: int (optional), override_params: object (optional model/temperature/max_tokens overrides). Loads the prompt template, renders variables from the input namespace, and runs an LLM completion. Output: {input, output, metrics: {cost, latency, tokens}}.

COMPLETION → model: str (LLM name, required, e.g. 'gpt-4o-mini'), temperature/max_tokens/top_p (optional). Sends input messages directly to the LLM without a template. Output: {input, output, metrics: {cost, latency, tokens}}.

THROTTLE → cooldown_seconds: int 1-86400 (required). Fires once per cooldown window and suppresses subsequent firings until the window elapses. Typical placement: after a threshold condition, before a notification/webhook, to prevent alert spam.

REPORT TASKS (type='reports' + trigger_event_type='scheduled' only; the digest window is anchored to the span since the previous scheduled fire):

GET_LOGS → window_seconds: int (required, ≤ 604800 = 7 days; fallback when no previous-fire anchor exists), metrics: array of DASHBOARD_METRICS names (required, e.g. number_of_requests, total_cost, total_tokens, error_count, error_percentage, average_cost, average_latency, average_ttft, unique_customers; max_tpm is rejected), group_by: array of bare CHLogV3 columns (organization_key_id, model, provider_id, environment, customer_identifier, prompt_id, status_code; empty = one summary row; a multi-element list is ONE composite grouping), breakdowns: array of column lists — independent per-dimension rollups, mutually exclusive with group_by (max 10), order_by: {field, direction} (optional, defaults first-metric desc), max_groups: int (default 100), include_prior_period: bool (adds prior-window totals for delta rendering). No custom metadata.X paths and no filtering — the slice is org + window.

GET_TRACES → trace-level sibling of get_logs over the trace agg table. window_seconds + metrics required; metrics from TRACE_METRICS (trace_count, total_cost, average_cost_per_trace, total_tokens, average_tokens_per_trace, error_count, average_duration, max_duration, average_spans_per_trace); group_by limited to organization_key_id, environment, customer_identifier (no model — a trace spans multiple models). No breakdowns / include_prior_period.

LIMIT_BREACHES → reports live limit-policy breaches at fire time (no window). scope: 'api_key' (only supported value, default), max_rows: int (default 50). Config may be empty {}.

GET_PULSE → pulls the report window's error-issue pulse facts for downstream summarization. max_issues: int (default 10), window_seconds: int (optional fallback when no previous-fire anchor — set to the same value as the report's get_logs tasks). Config may be empty {}.

PULSE_SUMMARIZE → LLM summary of upstream get_pulse facts. No config knobs — pass config {} and chain it directly after a get_pulse task.
